text:
Nicolas Roy was brought to Colorado to be the kind of center who makes a deep team deeper, and the underlying numbers say he's doing exactly that. The Avalanche take 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's on the ice at five on five, five points better than when he sits. For a player averaging under 13 minutes, that's the job done.

The production is modest, 4 goals and 4 assists in 18 games, and none of it on the power play. His shooting (16%) runs a bit above his talent range, but his chances are real: 4.35 expected goals already, a rate well above his last two seasons. His ice time has crept up lately, near 16 minutes in four of his last five games, with goals against Montreal and Anaheim.

He's not fast (15th percentile top speed) and doesn't need to be. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his zone exits leaving with possession last season. Watch whether the extra minutes stick.
headline: Roy is the quiet depth piece doing his job
